title: Multi-Future Drafting: Mixture Block Drafters for Tree-Verified Speculative Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2611.13017v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Block drafters such as DFlash draft a block of future tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees such as DDTree verify the prefixes ranked highest by the product of the drafter's per-position distributions. Under tree verification, the expected number of accepted tokens is the probability mass the tree covers. We show that a product misallocates it: when the continuation can follow several futures, it splices them into chimeras, prefixes stitched together from different futures that the target never produces, and gives them as much budget as the futures themselves. Barring ties, no product-ranked tree can hold two futures that disagree in $m$ positions without $2^{m-1}-1$ chimeras, however well the drafter is trained, and in practice chimeras make up 27-33% of a 64-node tree. We propose Multi-Future Drafting (MFD), which restores the coupling with a latent variable instead of the chain rule: $K$ learned mode embeddings at the drafter's

translated_title: 多未来草拟：面向树验证式推测解码的混合块草拟器
translated_abstract: 诸如DFlash之类的块草拟器可在一次前向传播中草拟一整块未来token，而诸如DDTree之类的草拟树则根据草拟器各位置分布的乘积对前缀进行排序并验证排名最高的前缀。在树验证机制下，期望接受的token数量等于树所覆盖的概率质量。我们证明乘积会错误地分配这一概率质量：当续写存在多个可能的未来路径时，乘积会将它们拼接成“嵌合体”（chimeras）——即由目标模型从不产生的、由不同未来拼接而成的前缀，并给予它们与真实未来同等的概率预算。除非出现平局，任何按乘积排序的树若要容纳两个在 $m$ 个位置上不一致的未来，就必然产生 $2^{m-1}-1$ 个嵌合体，无论草拟器训练得多好；在实践中，嵌合体占64节点树的27-33%。我们提出多未来草拟（MFD），它通过引入潜变量而非链式法则来恢复多个未来之间的耦合：在草拟器中设置 $K$ 个可学习的模式嵌入……
tldr: 论文揭示了基于乘积排序的草拟树在多未来场景下会将大量概率预算浪费在目标模型从不产生的“嵌合体”前缀上（占64节点树的27-33%），并提出多未来草拟（MFD），用潜变量（K个可学习模式嵌入）替代链式法则来恢复多个未来之间的耦合，从而提升树验证式推测解码的接受效率。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that product-ranked draft trees misallocate probability budget to "chimeras"—prefixes spliced from different futures that the target never produces (accounting for 27-33% of a 64-node tree)—and proposes Multi-Future Drafting (MFD), which restores the coupling between futures via a latent variable (K learned mode embeddings) instead of the chain rule, improving the efficiency of tree-verified speculative decoding.
